title: Pseudo-coherence on an affine scheme is pseudo-coherence of the module complex
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $M^\bullet$ be a complex of $A$-modules and let $E=\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ be the corresponding object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\subseteq D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] under the affine equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. Then $E$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] if and only if $M^\bullet$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 08E7 (perfect-lemma-pseudo-coherent-affine, perfect.tex line 2223), pseudo-coherent clause

proof.text: For the scheme-to-ring implication, choose standard derived categories for every localization ring. Apply [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-localization-cover] to obtain finitely many elements generating the unit ideal and pseudo-coherent localized complexes. Apply the pseudo-coherent clause (the second component) of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-localization-glue], with the unused fixed degree set to zero.

For the ring-to-scheme implication, unpack [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] to obtain a bounded-above finite-free complex E and an isomorphism Q(E) to Q(M). Obtain the affine derived equivalence and its termwise tilde comparison from [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. Map the isomorphism through the equivalence and the full-subcategory inclusion, then compose with the termwise comparison at M and E. This produces an isomorphism between the derived termwise tilde complexes.

Use the full open as the neighbourhood of every point in [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], and explicitly restrict termwise tilde(E) to its localized site. Additivity preserves zero terms above the bound. For each term, reindex the finite chosen module basis by ULift(Fin r); tildeFinsupp identifies its associated sheaf with the finite free sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. Restriction preserves the unit and finite coproducts, so SheafOfModules.mapFreeIso gives the required free-term isomorphism. Finally map the derived isomorphism through restriction and compose with Functor.mapDerivedCategoryFactors. All witnesses here are explicit complexes or proved basis constructions.
